newsitem.title: USA: No lie-detector test at British nanny murder trial.
newsitem.headline: No lie-detector test at British nanny murder trial.

text.p: The judge hearing the case of a British nanny accused of killing her charge ruled on Wednesday that a lie-detector test defence lawyers said proves she is telling the truth cannot be used at her trial.
Louise Woodward, 19, of Chester, England, was accused of killing Matthew Eappen in February.

The baby died as a result of severe head injuries. Police testified the teenager, who came to the United States last summer to work as an au pair, violently shook the infant and dropped him on the bathroom floor.
Middlesex Superior Court Judge Hiller Zobel, ruling from the bench after two-and-half days of pre-trial testimony, said the polygraph test "will not be admissable for any purpose at trial."
Zobel also set a new tentative trial date of Oct. 6. Woodward, who has been in custody at a state prison since her arrest in February, did not attend the hearings.
Woodward faces four different charges for the baby's death including murder in the first degree. If convicted, she could be sentenced to life in prison.
